features.name: Nothing published until both sign-offs are green
features.label: nothing published until both are green
features.promise: A publish cannot proceed until both the code review (screens 11 and 12) and the outcome sign-off (screen 13) have passed, and the publish carries both.
features.howToVerify: With a change whose code review is approved but whose outcome sign-off is not (and again with the reverse), open the publish step on screen 07 and confirm the destination choices cannot be committed; approve the second one and confirm the same publish then proceeds and shows both sign-offs attached.
features.notes: Flow map edge label 43:91 and the "Choose where it goes" caption 43:40 "Both sign-offs attached".
features.evidence: Walked the gate through three states on base's publish dialog and it refused every time short of two green answers. With no packet: the two distribution rows read 'This change has never been handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it. Push it for review first.' and were chipped 'Never handed over'. With the code approved against packet 1: 'The code review is signed off by Default Admin. The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding.', chipped 'Outcome sign-off outstanding'. With both recorded: chipped 'Needs a second signer' (see 00-cross-screen-two-signers). The submit stayed 'Pick a destination' and disabled throughout. The dialog also states that a weaker setting cannot loosen it: 'Settings put an outcome sign-off at "Notified". The gate takes both regardless, because this is the one boundary the design fixes, so the weaker value is recorded and not obeyed.' 'Load into this Rancher' is correctly ungated ('No sign-off'), which is the design's own rule that the gate sits at the distribution boundary only. I restored the record afterwards.

features.name: The brief sits on the main path before the build
features.label: Agree the brief — The need, the open questions, the criteria · Screen 10
features.promise: Agreeing the brief is a required stage between describing what you want (screen 02) and building it (screen 03), unlike checking the diff yourself (screen 04), which is explicitly optional.
features.howToVerify: Create a new extension from screen 02 and confirm the route passes through the brief on screen 10 before the workspace on screen 03; confirm by contrast that screen 04 can be skipped.
features.notes: Flow map: green connectors 43:50 and 43:53 put 43:11 between 43:8 and 43:16 on the main path, while 43:21 marks screen 04 "Optional". Rationale row 44:41: "It is only cheap to catch before the code exists".
features.evidence: Created an extension from screen 02 (description, outcome, name, 'Inside a cluster' placement). The submit button is literally labelled 'Draft the brief', and pressing it created the pod and routed to /dashboard/barn/extensions/<name>/brief?prompt=...&outcome=...&placement=c-cluster, so the brief sits between describing and building with the description carried into it. By contrast screen 04 is reachable but skippable: 'Keep and continue building' leaves it for the workspace with nothing signed and nothing blocked. I deleted the extension I created (deployment, service and both ConfigMaps).

features.name: No capability of the current build is lost
features.label: Keeps everything the current build does: CLI, files, GitHub import, publish, settings.
features.promise: The redesign is additive: the CLI, the files view, GitHub import, publish and settings all remain available, and the raw terminal output in particular is still reachable one click away and still the source of truth.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each of the five capabilities is still reachable in the running Studio, and that the raw assistant output is reachable in one click from the activity stream on screen 03.
features.notes: Cover point one (29:13); rationale row 27:16 "Raw output is still there, one click away, and still the source of truth".
features.evidence: Drove all five against the installed bundle, and the regression the last round found is gone. CLI: 'Show raw output' on screen 03 expands in one click and renders the pod's real log (vue-cli-service serve output with timestamps, 'DONE Compiled successfully in 2703ms'); the HTTP 406 is fixed, devServerLog now sends no Accept header and says why in a comment. The Terminal tab attaches a live xterm (canvas present) to the pod's tmux session, and I read my own prompts back out of it with `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor` three separate times. FILES: /barn/extensions/base/files lists the tree, marks NEW/EDITED and opens a file in the editor pane. GITHUB IMPORT: the Import dialog does connection as step one inside itself ('There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own to send you to'), with no link out to settings. PUBLISH: the dialog reads the version and the changed files out of the pod and lists each destination separately. SETTINGS: /barn/settings renders sign-off policy, GitHub connection, assistant permissions, preview target, access and what is sent to the model. Nothing regressed through the changed exec layer either: every write I made this run went through it and landed in the pod (a comment, a send-to-assistant, a per-file revert, a discard, a commit from Approve, a brief edit that rewrote BRIEF.md).

features.name: A requested change arrives as an assistant instruction
features.label: Goes straight back to the workspace with the comment already loaded into the assistant — the reviewer never writes the fix themselves
features.promise: A reviewer's comment, from either the code review or the outcome sign-off, is carried into the author's workspace already loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from, and the reviewer is never asked to write the fix.
features.howToVerify: Comment on a hunk on screen 12 and use "Send to the assistant", then open the author's workspace on screen 03 and confirm the reviewer's exact wording is present as a pending assistant instruction that the author must still approve.
features.notes: Flow map "Changes requested" (43:44/43:46) is fed by amber arrows from both "Code review" (43:82) and "Outcome sign-off" (43:85); rationale row 44:32 adds "the author still approves it".
features.evidence: Two routes, both land in the same place. From a hunk: 'Send to the assistant' put my exact sentence into the pod's session ('Their words: w5-review-cross probe: send this one to the assistant please.. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.'). From the decision bar: 'Request changes' recorded the rejection and then routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal, with the pane holding 'A reviewer looked at the working tree of the base extension and asked for a change: <my paragraph>. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.' The reviewer writes a sentence, not a fix, and the author still has to act on it.

features.name: One diff against the last published version
features.label: collapsed into one diff against the last published version
features.promise: The reviewer is shown a single diff of the change against the last published version, not the sequence of intermediate edits that produced it.
features.howToVerify: Make an edit and then undo or supersede it before pushing, then open the change on screen 12 and confirm the diff shows only the net difference from the last published version and no intermediate state.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.evidence: Built the case on demo: set refs/barn/published/local to the then-HEAD, committed verify-w5-committed.md, and left verify-w5-working.md uncommitted. The review screen showed one diff of two files measured from that baseline, with no per-commit history and no intermediate state, and named the point out loud ('this list is measured against the last version published into this Rancher'). Screen 12 says the same thing when narrowing: 'The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 2 files.' I reset demo afterwards.

features.name: Connection state and permission mode are one state shown in two places
features.label: Connection state is a persistent strip in the panel: a dot, the account, and the permission mode as a real control.
features.promise: The account, connection state and assistant permission mode shown on the workspace strip (screen 03) and on the settings page (screen 09) are the same state, and settings is the one place all of it lives.
features.howToVerify: Change the permission mode on screen 09 and confirm the workspace strip on screen 03 reflects it without a reload, and vice versa; confirm no other modal edits the GitHub token.
features.notes: Rationale rows 27:25 ("Screens 03, 09") and 27:34; caption 23:918 "connection, permissions, access and data in one place", replacing the bare token modal (23:919).
features.defect: Two defects against this rule. (1) The permission mode is not one state in two places: screen 03 sets the live session's mode and screen 09 reports the pod's start-up mode, and after changing it on 03 the two disagreed with no indication that they are different things. (2) A second surface still edits the GitHub token: the editor settings modal opened from [data-testid=barn-editor-settings-button] on screen 03 contains a password field [data-testid=barn-settings-token] placeholder 'ghp_...' that writes the token, alongside screen 09's own connection card. That modal is the 'bare GitHub token modal' the redesign says it replaces.
features.evidence: Drove the permission mode in both directions. Screen 03's strip chip is a real control: its menu offers 'Edits apply without asking', 'File edits apply, everything else asks', 'Planning only, no edits' and 'claude decides what to ask about', and picking the second one changed the chip. Screen 09 did not follow: its radio group still had 'Do not ask at all' checked afterwards, and the group is explicitly marked not settable ([data-testid=settings-permission-fixed], 'Not settable, and not per user. The pod starts claude...'). Clicking a different radio there changes nothing.

features.name: Verification walks the criteria written in the brief
features.label: Acceptance criteria written in the brief become a checklist walked against the running build, with captured evidence and a second, separate sign-off.
features.promise: The acceptance criteria are authored once on screen 10 and are the same items walked, against the running build and with evidence captured, on screen 13.
features.howToVerify: Write a distinctive acceptance criterion in the brief on screen 10, take the change through to verification, and confirm screen 13 lists that exact criterion as a checklist item, exercised against the running build, with the captured evidence attached.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59 ("Screens 07 and 13"); caption 45:1206 "the criteria walked against the running build"; flow map 43:37.
features.evidence: Wrote a distinctive criterion on screen 10 ('w5rc marker criterion: the queue lists only handed-over work') into the fourth Acceptance criterion field; the page saved it ('Saved 11:07 PM') and BRIEF.md in the pod gained '- [ ] w5rc marker criterion...' under '## How we will know it worked'. Screen 12 then listed it verbatim among its four criteria with the state 'not measured', and screen 13 listed it as item 4 of the walked checklist with Yes / No / Can't tell / Show me against it. Nothing was re-entered anywhere. I restored BRIEF.md byte for byte afterwards (md5 matches the backup).

features.name: Built from components the dashboard already has
features.label: Everything below is achievable with components that already exist in the Rancher dashboard — SortableTable, LabeledInput, Banner, Card, Tabbed, AsyncButton — so none of this asks the team to invent new UI primitives.
features.promise: Every screen is realisable with existing Rancher dashboard primitives, and the Studio home list in particular uses the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page rather than a bespoke table.
features.howToVerify: Inspect the rendered markup of the Studio screens and confirm tables, inputs, banners, cards, tabs and async buttons are the dashboard's own components rather than reimplementations, and that screen 01 reads like the Clusters page table.
features.notes: Header note 27:5 of the rationale frame; rationale row 27:88 names the Clusters page pattern for screen 01.
features.defect: Screen 01 is a bespoke table, not the SortableTable pattern the rationale row names ('the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page'), so the claim that a Rancher user already knows how to read it does not hold. The wider claim is met in spirit (nothing needs a new primitive) but not in fact (the primitives are new implementations of existing ones).
features.evidence: Inspected the rendered markup. The Studio is built from its own S-prefixed primitives in pkg/barn/components/ui (SButton, SChip, SBanner, SCard, STabs, SMenu, SModal), not from the dashboard's. Screen 01's table is a div grid with class 'studio-home__table' and hand-rolled 'studio-home__th' headers: document.querySelector('.sortable-table') is null and no element under it carries a sortable-table class.

features.name: A guaranteed way back from any build failure
features.label: When it breaks — plain-language cause, one-click fix, guaranteed way back
features.promise: Every build is snapshotted so that a failure always has a state to roll back to, which means the snapshot has to be taken in the workspace before the change that breaks it.
features.howToVerify: Cause a build to fail from a known-good state and confirm screen 08 offers a snapshot of that state to roll back to, and that rolling back returns the workspace to it.
features.notes: Caption 23:915 and rationale row 27:97 "a snapshot to roll back to"; the snapshot is created on screen 03 and consumed on screen 08.
features.evidence: Seeded a recorded failure and opened screen 08. It named the cause in words, offered 'Ask the assistant to explain this', 'Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue' and, for the way back, 'Roll back to the snapshot "autosave 2314 on Aug 23"' taken 25 seconds earlier, with 'Undo the last change' beside it. The snapshots are real: refs/tags/barn-snap/* in the pod holds dozens of automatic ones, so a failure always has a point to return to. The screen is also honest about the limit of the guarantee rather than overselling it: 'no build of this extension has succeeded here yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a build that is known to have worked', and 'Rolling back snapshots the failed tree first, so nothing you have done is lost'. I did not press it, since a rollback would take other verifiers' work with it.

features.name: Iteration before the gate asks nobody
features.label: Iteration is completely ungated: dev preview and developer load ask nobody.
features.promise: Creating, building, previewing, breaking, rebuilding and developer-loading an extension never require anyone's approval, so no review or sign-off control may block any of them.
features.howToVerify: Make several edits in the workspace (screen 03), let a build fail and recover it (screen 08), and developer-load the result, confirming that no approval dialog, pending-review banner or disabled control appears at any point before screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 65:1083; flow map caption 43:18 "Readable activity, live preview, and no gates at all" and 43:24 "Everything before it is yours alone".
features.evidence: Everything I did before the publish dialog asked nobody. Created an extension, wrote and reverted files, discarded a whole working tree, switched diff modes, commented, sent a comment to the assistant, opened the live preview, edited the brief and opened the failure screen with its rollback offer, on three different extensions. No approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control appeared at any point. The only 'Requires approval' and 'The gate' chips in the product are on the two distribution rows of the publish dialog, and the local install row is chipped 'No sign-off'.

features.name: The OCI publish gate
features.label: Push to an OCI repository — The one hard gate. Everything before it is yours alone · Screen 07
features.promise: There is exactly one hard gate in the whole product and it is the push to an OCI repository, the point at which the extension first becomes installable by other people.
features.howToVerify: From a freshly created extension, walk stages 01, 02, 10, 03 and 04 without ever being asked for an approval, then start a publish to an OCI repository on screen 07 and confirm that this is the first and only step that will not complete on the author's say-so alone.
features.notes: Flow map 43:22/43:24 and the guardrail note 43:93; rationale row 65:1083 states it as "The gate is the push to an OCI repository, where the extension first becomes installable by other people".
features.evidence: The publish dialog names exactly one hard gate and puts it at the distribution boundary: 'Push to an OCI repository. The gate. The one hard gate in the design: the point an extension becomes installable by people who did not build it, and the only step that asks anybody for permission.' 'Load into this Rancher' beside it is chipped 'No sign-off' and reversible ('"Remove local install" takes it back off'). Nothing earlier in the walk (01, 02, 10, 03, 04) asked for an approval. The OCI push itself is not built and the dialog says so plainly rather than drawing a button that lies: 'The gate in front of it works; the push itself does not exist, and a button that pretended otherwise would be worse than this sentence.'

features.name: The hand-off to review is a PR, and the PR is the record
features.label: hand-off · the PR is the record
features.promise: Crossing the gate hands the work from the author's lane to the reviewers' lane by producing a PR, and that PR is the durable record of the hand-off.
features.howToVerify: Push a change to an OCI repository and confirm the resulting queue entry on screen 11 is backed by a PR, and that the PR is reachable from the review surface as the record of the change.
features.notes: Flow map connector label 43:90 on the green connector running from "Push to an OCI repository" (43:22) into "Code review" (43:28).
features.defect: Neither route across the gate can create the PR in this product as installed. 'Push to an OCI repository' is 'Not built' by the dialog's own admission, and 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' / 'Push the source to GitHub' needs a GitHub token that Studio has no way to obtain by itself ('There is no "Authorise with GitHub" because Studio has no OAuth app of its own'). So the hand-off record the flow map calls 'the PR is the record' cannot be produced by the one hard gate at all, and the seeded packet on base carries pr: null.
features.evidence: The reading half is now right and it is this round's fix: the chip and the queue read the PR out of the packet record rather than from the branch, so they work with no token and would survive the PR being merged (packet.pr is rendered by queue-pr-<name> and by rc-pr, and where there is no packet the chip says 'Not handed over yet'). What I could not do is produce the record, because crossing the gate produces nothing here.

features.name: Preview and published are separated by an explicit line
features.label: The same live preview, plus an explicit boundary: preview is yours alone, snapshotted per build, and publishing is a separate deliberate act.
features.promise: Work in the live preview affects only the author and is snapshotted per build; nothing reaches anyone else until the separate, deliberate publish on screen 07.
features.howToVerify: Make a visible change in the workspace preview on screen 03, then confirm from another session or another user that the installed extension is unchanged until a publish is performed on screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 27:52 ("Screens 03, 07"); the cover's reading note 29:41 calls it "an explicit line between preview and published".
features.evidence: base has had a dirty working tree throughout this run and nothing about it reached anybody: `kubectl get uiplugins -A` lists only barn and nodehealth, and base's own row on screen 01 offers 'Remove the local install' greyed out with the reason 'not installed'. The review screen says the same in words ('These changes are running in your preview only', 'Nothing here has reached the repository yet'), and publishing is a separate deliberate act behind a confirmation modal that spells out the consequence ('Everybody signed into this cluster gets the new build the next time they load a page'). Snapshots are taken per build (refs/tags/barn-snap/*, the newest 25 seconds old when I looked).

features.name: Prompt provenance and the brief survive from authoring into review
features.label: Every hunk carries the prompt that produced it, and the whole change carries its brief.
features.promise: The prompt that caused each hunk is captured during authoring on screen 03 and is still attached, per hunk, when the change is reviewed on screen 12, and the brief from screen 10 travels with the change as a whole.
features.howToVerify: Author a change with two distinguishable prompts in the workspace, push it, then on screen 12 confirm each hunk shows the prompt that produced it and that the change header shows the brief written on screen 10.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:5; caption 45:1204 "prompt provenance per hunk".
features.defect: no detail given
features.evidence: The path exists end to end in the product (provenanceFor() blames each line back to the turn that committed it, the strip renders per hunk, the brief travels with the change and is shown in the packet column, and I proved the brief half by writing a criterion on screen 10 and reading it back on 12 and 13). The prompt half cannot be exercised: claude in every pod in this cluster answers 'Not logged in . Please run /login', so no turn can run, nothing can commit a turn id, and both pods report no provenance ('this pod was started before the Studio recorded provenance' on nodehealth, 'no prompt recorded' on base). Authoring a change with two distinguishable prompts is not possible until the pod's assistant is signed in.

features.name: Live is reversible from the extension list
features.label: Reversible from the extension list
features.promise: Publishing is not a one-way door: a live extension can be taken back from the Studio home list on screen 01.
features.howToVerify: Publish an extension, return to /dashboard/barn/extensions, and confirm the row for the live extension offers a way to reverse the publish.
features.notes: Flow map terminal state "Live" (43:41) and its caption 43:43; the reversal control lives on screen 01, not on screen 07.
features.evidence: Opened the row menu for each extension on /barn/extensions. nodehealth, which is installed as a UIPlugin (cattle-ui-plugin-system/nodehealth v0.1.0), offers an enabled 'Remove the local install v0.1.0'. base and demo, which are not installed, show the same item disabled with the reason on it ('not installed'). So the list is where a live extension is taken back, and the item states its own applicability rather than being hidden.

features.name: Every recovery route returns to the same workspace
features.label: amber is recovery — and every recovery route leads back into the same workspace rather than out of the product
features.promise: Both failure routes drawn on the map, a broken build and a rejected review, end back in the author's workspace rather than in a separate remediation surface or outside the product.
features.howToVerify: Trigger a build failure and apply its fix, confirming the user lands back in the same workspace; separately, request changes as a reviewer and confirm the author is returned to that same workspace rather than to a new screen.
features.notes: Flow map legend 43:4; the amber arrows 43:62/43:65 leave and re-enter the same "Build it and watch it" box (43:16), and "Changes requested" (43:44) routes back to it.
features.evidence: Both amber routes end in the same workspace. Rejection: 'Request changes' on screen 12 routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the comment already in the assistant's session, not to a remediation screen. Build failure: screen 08's actions are all workspace actions ('Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Undo the last change', 'Roll back to the snapshot'), and its own copy is about returning the same tree rather than branching out of the product. Neither route left the Studio.

features.name: The review packet accumulates in the background and is assembled at the push
features.label: the review packet accumulates quietly in the background. It is only assembled and handed to a reviewer at the push to a repository
features.promise: Everything a reviewer will need is captured continuously while the author works, but it is only assembled into a review packet and handed over at the moment of the push.
features.howToVerify: Work in the workspace for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue (screen 11), then push once and confirm a complete packet, including material captured across all of those earlier cycles, appears in a single queue entry.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: Nothing accumulates in the background while the author works. The one material the packet is supposed to have gathered across earlier cycles is the per-hunk prompt provenance, and the packet on base carries none (screen 12 reports 'No prompt recorded for any of this change's 39 lines'). The assembly at the push cannot be exercised either, for the reason in 00-cross-screen-pr-is-the-record. Also worth fixing in the fixture: barn-review-base names packet 1 at refs/barn/packets/1 but the pod has no such ref, so distributionGate() reads the extension as never handed over while the queue and screen 12 show packet 1. I added the ref temporarily to test the gate and removed it again.
features.evidence: The queue half is fixed this round and I confirmed it: handedOverExtensions() filters the enumeration, so demo and nodehealth, both with dirty working trees, are not in anybody's queue, and the empty state says why in the rule's own terms ('2 extensions in this Rancher have work in the author's own tree, which is not a review request: a change arrives here when it is pushed for review as a packet'). Only base, which has a packet, is listed. What is not there is the accumulation.

features.name: The build is compared back to its own brief at sign-off
features.label: The build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged during sign-off — accept it into the brief, or take it out.
features.promise: At outcome sign-off the built change is diffed against the brief that started it, and anything not in the brief is surfaced with two resolutions: accept it into the brief, or remove it.
features.howToVerify: Have the assistant make a change beyond what the brief asked for, take it to screen 13, and confirm the extra work is flagged as outside the brief and offers both accepting it into the brief and taking it out.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:68; requires the screen 10 brief to still be attached to the change at screen 13.
features.evidence: Now works. Put a file in the pod whose added line mentions words the brief ruled out ('// w5rc scope probe: alerting and history beyond the brief'). Screen 13's Scope section flagged it: 'This change adds lines that mention what the brief said it was deliberately not doing', listing alerting, history and beyond against verify-w5-scope.ts, each with both resolutions as real buttons: 'That is fine - add it to the brief' and 'Remove it'. It also explains what each does ('Accepting rewrites BRIEF.md: the sentence that ruled this out moves into What changes for them, stamped with today's date' / 'Removing it does not touch the brief - it puts the behaviour to the assistant in this extension's pod and asks for it back out') and states its own limit rather than implying it read the change. Removed the file afterwards.

features.name: Re-review is incremental across visits
features.label: A "since your last look" filter, and a banner on the queue row saying how many changes landed since you approved.
features.promise: Per-reviewer state persists between visits, so a reviewer returning after the author has pushed again sees how many changes landed since they approved and can filter the diff to just those.
features.howToVerify: Approve a change as a reviewer, push further changes as the author, then return to screen 11 and confirm the queue row banners the number of changes since that approval, and that screen 12 offers a "since your last look" filter restricted to them.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:23, "Screens 11 and 12".
features.evidence: Per-reviewer state persists and both screens use it. Opening screen 12 recorded a look under my principal in barn-review-base ('looks': {pa5g3hz: {principal: local://user-btc48, sha: 24b3922, at: ...}}), which survived reloads and navigations. The queue row then carried the re-review banner with the count sentence, and its 'Show only what changed since then' link opened screen 12 at ?scope=since&from=<sha> with the chip already active and the diff narrowed from 2 files to 1.

features.name: Two sign-offs by two different people
features.label: Splits "is it safe?" from "does it work?" — two questions, two people, neither able to answer the other's.
features.promise: The code review is signed by a developer and the outcome sign-off by the person who asked for the change; they are separate acts by separate roles, not one approval recorded twice.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the code review record (screen 12) and the verification record (screen 13) carry distinct signer identities and distinct timestamps, and that signing one does not mark the other complete.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59; flow map 43:32 "A developer" and 43:37 "The person who asked"; cover point three 29:21 "a separate outcome sign-off by the person who asked".
features.evidence: Recorded both sign-offs against packet 1 with the same principal and the gate refused: 'Both sign-offs on packet 1 carry the same person, Default Admin. The two questions are "is it safe?" and "does it work?", and they are two sign-offs precisely because one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice.', with the destination chipped 'Needs a second signer'. With two different principals the same packet moved into the 'Signed off this week' tab instead. The two records are separate objects with their own verdict, principal, name, time and commit, and signing the code left the outcome gate open on screen 12's decision bar. Restored the record afterwards.

features.name: Actions column header (blank)
features.promise: The final column has no header text and no sort glyph, because it holds per-row actions.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the last column header is empty and offers no sort control.
features.evidence: The last column header renders as <button class="studio-home__th studio-home__th--plain"> with empty text and no .studio-home__sort glyph (the other five all carry one). Nit rather than a defect: it is still a button wired to toggleSort({id:'actions'}), and pressing it moves the sorted indicator off whatever column had it while leaving the row order at the name tie-break, because sortValue returns '' for every row on that key.

features.name: Breadcrumb: Studio (current)
features.label: Studio
features.promise: The trailing crumb names the page the user is on and is not a link.
features.howToVerify: Confirm 'Studio' renders after the chevron and does not navigate on click.
features.evidence: The trailing crumb is Studio - no anchor, no handler. Force-clicked it from /dashboard/barn/extensions and the URL was unchanged afterwards.

features.name: Breadcrumb: Extensions
features.label: Extensions
features.promise: The 'Extensions' crumb navigates up to the Rancher Extensions page.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Extensions' in the breadcrumb above the title and confirm the Rancher Extensions page loads.
features.notes: Followed by a chevron and the non-clickable current crumb 'Studio'.
features.evidence: [data-testid=studio-crumb-extensions] is the 'Extensions' anchor. Clicked it and landed on /dashboard/c/local/uiplugins#installed, Rancher's own Extensions page.

features.name: Extension count pill
features.promise: A pill beside the title shows how many extensions the table holds.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the pill next to the title shows the number of rows in the table, and that it tracks the filter when the search box is used.
features.notes: The design shows 6 with 6 rows drawn. Whether the count reflects the filtered set or the total is not stated.
features.evidence: The pill beside the title read 3 with title '3 extensions'. Typing 'node' took it to 1, 'zzzznomatch' to 0, clearing back to 3; after I created a fourth extension it read 4. It tracks the filtered set, not the raw one.

features.name: Filter extensions
features.label: Filter
features.promise: A bordered search box with a magnifier icon lets the user type text to narrow the extension table.

features.name: Choose which model answers
features.label: Claude Opus 5
features.promise: A chip inside the composer names the model the assistant will use, implying you can pick a different one.
features.howToVerify: From https://magic-closet-rancher/dashboard/barn/editor click the 'Claude Opus 5' chip and check a model list opens; pick another model and check the chip label changes and the next turn uses it.
features.notes: chip with icon/sparkle (5:83), text 11:345. No chevron is drawn, so it may only be a badge showing the active model. Selectability is inferred from its placement in the composer's action bar.
features.evidence: Implemented this round, and it is both an honest reading and a working picker. Standing state: the chip reads "Default model", title "Nothing in this pod names a model: no --model on the claude that is running, no ANTHROPIC_MODEL in its environment, and no `model` in claude's settings" - and that is true, /app/.home/.claude/settings.json had no model key. Clicking it opened a menu of the aliases the pod's own claude --help documents (fable, opus, sonnet) plus "Choose in the terminal /model". Picking sonnet: the chip relabelled to "sonnet" and /app/.home/.claude/settings.json in the pod gained "model": "sonnet". I removed the key again afterwards and the chip went back to "Default model". ONE DEFECT worth fixing, which did not stop the pass: assistantModel() in extensions.ts destructures `section('--settings--', '--help--').split('\n')` straight into [settings, config], but element 0 is the empty tail of the `echo --settings--` line, so settings is always '', the settings.json value is reported as coming from ~/.claude.json (the tooltip said "Read from `model` in the pod's ~/.claude.json" when the value was in ~/.claude/settings.json), and a model set only in ~/.claude.json is dropped entirely. Filter the empty leading line before destructuring.
